old: The selected ISO/IEC 25010:2023 characteristics remain Functional Suitability, Performance Efficiency, Interaction Capability, Reliability, and Security, as defined in Chapters I and II. Automated functional and access checks provide limited technical evidence; they do not by themselves establish scores for all five characteristics. new:
The selected ISO/IEC 25010:2023 characteristics remain Functional Suitability, Performance Efficiency, Interaction Capability, Reliability, and Security, as defined in Chapters I and II. Each characteristic requires evidence appropriate to its purpose; a passed automated suite does not establish a score for every characteristic.

Functional Suitability is supported by recorded checks of intake, validation, allocation, correction handling, rent confirmation, receipt access, and personal utility tracking. These results apply to the exercised cases. Representative extraction accuracy still requires a declared sample set and manually checked reference values.

Performance Efficiency has not yet been established through a controlled response-time, resource-use, or concurrent-user study. The full-suite duration reported in Section 3.2.3 measures the time taken by the test suite and must not be presented as bill-processing latency or evidence of production capacity.

Interaction Capability has preliminary evidence from automated browser journeys and phone-sized layout checks. These checks do not replace actual-device tasks, participant feedback, or an adviser-approved usability questionnaire. The proposed interface redesign remains separate from the implemented screens and must be checked after application.

Reliability is supported by the recorded duplicate, replay, restart-persistence, invalid-correction rollback, and independent-job failure scenarios. These bounded checks do not establish long-term availability or operation while the server is shut down.

Security has evidence from selected authentication, role, record-access, and workspace-isolation checks. It has not been established through a complete penetration test or legal compliance audit. No questionnaire ratings, respondent counts, OCR accuracy percentage, load capacity, or security certification are reported as completed results.

old: Once billing information has been extracted, it must be checked and processed according to defined conditions. Rule-based processing uses explicit conditions and decision rules to classify, validate, and route information. Wu et al. (2022) demonstrate the use of rule-based information extraction to organize domain-specific information, while Baralis et al. (2022) discuss business-rule engines for representing and executing operational decisions in a structured manner. Extending this idea to process automation, Geyer-Klingeberg et al. (2024) present a rule-based method that analyzes decision logic and classifies business processes according to their suitability for robotic process automation, while Kim et al. (2011) examine proactive exception handling in business processes. These studies support the use of predefined and traceable conditions to determine whether a record proceeds through normal processing or requires additional review. Applying these principles, the proposed system uses defined rules for billing validation, provider and account/reference mapping, duplicate detection, and identifying individual or shared billing arrangements. Records that do not meet the defined conditions are sent to the Exception Queue for Staff investigation and, when required, Manager decisions. These rules, together with the separation between Tenant-reported rent and Manager-confirmed rent status, are system requirements rather than findings established by the cited studies. Digital rent receipts are created only after Manager confirmation. Personal utility tracking remains separate and does not establish provider settlement.

section: Web Push, Rent Email Notifications, and Secure Notification Delivery, paragraph 1
old: After a billing record is finalized, tenants need to be informed that their billing information is available. The World Wide Web Consortium (2024a) describes the Push API, including push services and user subscriptions. The World Wide Web Consortium (2024b) also explains the role of service workers in handling web events in the background when they are included in the system implementation. Because Web Push involves browser subscriptions and authorization, security must also be considered. Carboneri et al. (2023) examine Web Push implementations in the wild and identify security concerns involving push subscriptions and authorization. In the proposed system, Web Push Notifications serve as billing alerts that direct tenants to the authenticated web portal, where complete billing information is available. However, Web Push does not confirm payment, prove that payment occurred, or show whether the tenant read the notification. Tenant payment reporting therefore remains separate from Manager confirmation.

section: Software Quality Evaluation and Security, paragraph 1
old: To evaluate the proposed system systematically, the study requires defined software-quality criteria. ISO/IEC 25010:2023 provides a product-quality model for systems and software quality requirements and evaluation (International Organization for Standardization, 2023). Guided by this model, the study will evaluate five quality characteristics: Functional Suitability, Performance Efficiency, Interaction Capability, Reliability, and Security. These characteristics provide a basis for examining whether the system performs its intended functions, performs efficiently, supports user interaction, operates consistently, and protects information. Security is particularly important because the system handles tenant and billing information. Republic Act No. 10173, or the Data Privacy Act of 2012, requires organizations that process personal information to use reasonable and appropriate measures to protect it (Republic of the Philippines, 2012). The National Privacy Commission (2016) further discusses safeguards for the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of personal data, while Zafar et al. (2022) review authorization and access-control strategies that restrict system functions and information according to user permissions. In the proposed system, role-based access separates Admin maintenance, Staff operations, Manager authorization, and Tenant-own functions. Rent email notifications will use authorized recipient records, protected sending credentials, and limited message content that directs tenants to the authenticated portal. These sources guide the study’s quality and security evaluation, but they do not prove that the system already meets the selected quality characteristics or privacy requirements. The Security evaluation is limited to the defined system functions, access controls, and security-related criteria included in the study’s evaluation procedures. It does not constitute a legal audit, certification, or claim of complete compliance with the Philippine Data Privacy Act.

old: The centralized database shall retain property, unit, Tenant, mapping, rent, billing, rent-payment, utility-tracking, exception, correction, receipt, and applicable notification records. Rent bills shall use Unpaid, Tenant Reported Paid, and Paid. Tenant reports shall remain unconfirmed until Manager confirmation; the Manager may also record and confirm an actual rent payment without a prior report after external checking. Receipts shall be issued only for confirmed rent payments. Utilities shall use separate Not Marked Paid and Self-Reported Paid tracking labels, with the notice “Provider payment not verified.” Each utility mark shall belong to the reporting Tenant and the corresponding bill or allocated share, without authorizing a system-issued receipt or changing other tenants' marks. Tenants shall access their bills, stored portal notifications, history, rent statuses, personal utility tracking, and confirmed rent receipts through the authenticated portal. Eligible reminders shall be scheduled at 9 AM Philippine time, three calendar days before the actual due date. Routine valid billing records shall proceed automatically, while exceptions shall require Manager intervention. Web Push shall provide permitted rent and utility alerts. Supplementary email notifications shall cover rent billing updates, eligible rent reminders, and Manager-confirmed rent payment notices only. Outgoing rent email shall be separate from utility-email intake. The system shall use the Tenant's registered email address and retain queued events, channel-specific attempts, and available acceptance or failure results. Limited retries and duplicate controls shall prevent repeated sends during normal processing. Sending failure shall not change payment status or prevent portal access. SMS, GSM, and utility email notifications shall not be used.

new:
The current development verification was conducted on 28 October 2026 using an Acer TravelMate P215-53 laptop with an Intel Core i5-1135G7 processor at 2.40 GHz, four physical cores, eight logical processors, and approximately 7.78 GiB of system-reported physical memory. The operating system was Windows 11 Pro, 64-bit, version 10.0.26200, build 26200. These specifications describe the current run and are not assumed to describe earlier test runs.

The software environment used Node.js 24.21.0, SQLite 3.53.4, and the existing HTML, CSS, and JavaScript frontend. Automated browser tasks used Playwright 1.64.0 with headless Microsoft Edge 156.0.4314.50. Extraction used PDF.js 6.2.108 and Tesseract.js 6.0.1. The installed communication packages were MailParser 3.9.38, ImapFlow 1.7.8, Nodemailer 10.1.0, and web-push 3.6.7. Installed versions, source hashes, fixture hashes, individual observations, and procedures are retained in the dated development-evidence file.

The full suite ran one test file at a time. Measurements were collected separately after other automated test jobs finished, and the suite was then rerun after correcting a date-dependent test expectation. Scheduled production processing and external mail or Push delivery were not enabled for the measurements. Normal operating-system background activity was not fully controlled.

section: 3.2.3, measured development observations before the dated Gmail paragraph
old: A separate controlled Gmail test on 23 October 2026
newPrefix:
Local response measurements used the authenticated reports-summary endpoint and a disposable file-backed SQLite database containing 4 properties, 4 units, 3 tenants, and 30 bills, with no payments or receipts. After five warm-up requests excluded from the measurements, 50 requests were sent sequentially. A second group used five concurrent request loops, each sending ten requests to the already warmed server. Timing started before each request and ended after the complete response body was read. The 95th percentile used the nearest-rank method.

For the sequential group, the mean response time was 5.23 milliseconds, the median was 4.67 milliseconds, and the 95th percentile was 8.50 milliseconds. For the five-loop group, the corresponding values were 23.29, 23.19, and 32.78 milliseconds. All 100 measured requests returned successful HTTP responses with readable JSON. The maximum sampled memory reading across both groups was approximately 181.90 MiB for the Node evidence process and its in-process server. section: Chapter I, Section 1.5, paragraphs 1-9 replaced with five paragraphs
reason: Concise scope and final manuscript alignment; no new system feature or evaluation claim
old:
The study will develop and evaluate a web-based property-management workflow for selected boarding houses and residential apartments in Pasig City during Academic Year 2026-2027. It will centralize property, unit, tenant, utility-mapping, rent, billing, payment, exception, correction, receipt, and notification records. “Intelligent” refers to OCR text extraction combined with explicit, deterministic, and traceable processing rules. An existing OCR engine may use machine-learning-based recognition, but the researchers will not train or customize a model. Validation, classification, computation, allocation and payment decisions will follow predefined rules and Manager-controlled actions rather than autonomous AI decisions.

Billing will cover rent, electricity, and water only. Rent will be fixed and non-prorated, generated once per monthly anniversary cycle with the same due date. Short months will use their final day while preserving the original anniversary day for later months. After an outage, missed eligible cycles will be generated once with their original due dates and actual creation dates retained. The first bill will show current rent and one-month advance separately. Confirmed advance will be reserved for the final applicable rent cycle and applied only with Manager confirmation, using the original payment and receipt without another cash transaction or duplicate receipt. Applied credit cannot be reused, and no replacement advance will be charged automatically. Individual charges will follow the configured lease or utility account. Shared charges will be split equally among eligible tenants in the Manager-configured group, with two-decimal shares totaling the source charge. Tenants will choose the payer of a shared provider bill outside the system; allocation will not represent contribution collection or verified provider settlement.

The system will support month-to-month rentals that continue until the Tenant leaves. The Manager will record the rental start date and leave the end date blank while occupancy continues. The end date will be recorded when the Tenant leaves. Rent will follow the monthly anniversary rule, with no new cycles generated after the recorded end date. The existing Tenant account will retain access to its own bills, utility tracking history, confirmed payments, and receipts, and unpaid balances will not be removed merely because occupancy has ended. Departed tenants may report outstanding rent payments for Manager confirmation. Advance rent will equal one month of the Tenant's configured rent or, for shared rent, the Tenant's calculated rent share at the time the advance is charged. Its amount will not be entered as an arbitrary credit allowance. A later change in rent or shared allocation that causes a credit mismatch will require Manager review. Automatic unit transfers and lease-renewal processing will not be included in the study.

Utility bills will enter the system through supported email-body summaries and attachments received by the designated property-management email account, or through optional Staff or Manager uploads of clear photographs or scans of printed provider bills. The Manager may hand a printed bill directly to tenants without uploading it. Until a supported email or uploaded copy is received and validated, that bill will not be available in the portal for automatic allocation, personal tracking, history, or reminders. Readable email summaries and digitally generated PDFs will use direct text extraction, while clear bill images will use OCR. The five target fields will remain the amount due, due date, billing period, provider, and account or reference identifier. Processing will be limited to selected provider formats; the availability of a provider email, PDF attachment, or complete identifier will not be assumed. Required-field, mapping, period, and duplicate checks will precede classification and computation across all supported intake methods. Masked or incomplete identifiers will require Manager review against verified account information; the system will not infer hidden characters or assign a bill by guessing. Incomplete, uncertain, duplicated, unmappable, or otherwise invalid records will enter the Exception Queue for Staff investigation or Manager correction. Staff correction proposals will require Manager authorization, and accepted corrections will undergo system revalidation and reprocessing. Finalized corrections will preserve prior values and tracking history. Utility due dates will come from validated received billing information; the system will not predict the next billing period's due date.

Rent payment statuses will remain Unpaid, Tenant Reported Paid, and Paid. Tenants may report rent payments for Manager review. The Manager may also record and confirm an actual rent payment without a prior Tenant report, after checking it outside the system. Only the Manager may authorize confirmed rent receipts; rejected reports will return to Unpaid with a recorded reason. Utilities will use a separate Tenant-controlled tracker with Not Marked Paid and Self-Reported Paid, accompanied by “Provider payment not verified.” A mark will refer only to the Tenant's own utility bill or allocated share and will neither require Manager confirmation nor generate a system-issued utility receipt. For shared bills, one Tenant's mark will not mark other shares or the whole provider account as paid. The system will not independently verify payments. Tenants will access their billing history, rent statuses, utility tracking records, and confirmed rent receipts through the authenticated portal.

Portal notifications will retain billing alerts that tenants can view after login. Web Push will provide rent and utility billing updates and eligible reminders. Supplementary email notifications will be limited to rent billing updates, eligible rent reminders, and Manager-confirmed rent payment notices sent to the Tenant's registered email address. Both channels will direct tenants to the authenticated portal; emails will not create another payment or receipt. Reminders will be scheduled at 9 AM Philippine time, three calendar days before the actual due date, for eligible Unpaid rent and utility records Not Marked Paid. Pending rent reports and utilities marked Self-Reported Paid will be excluded; utility reminders will use Web Push only. Bills unavailable before the scheduled reminder time, including rent generated on its due date, will receive billing updates rather than backdated reminders. A missed reminder will not be sent retrospectively. Email sending will require internet connectivity, configured sending credentials, and a running backend. Sending attempts and available channel acceptance or failure results will be recorded, with limited retries and duplicate prevention. Push permission, device support, unavailable email configuration, or delivery failure will not prevent portal access. An alert will not prove payment, inbox delivery, or readership. Tenant SMS and utility email notifications are excluded.

Admin will manage accounts and system maintenance, including authorized role and workspace assignments. Admin may also inspect permitted profile, contact, unit, bill, allocation, rent-status and system-generated rent receipt records across workspaces through a read-only view. This view will exclude private uploaded files, original utility sources, raw extraction, full utility account references and authentication details. Admin will not edit operational or financial records, confirm rent, decide correction proposals or change Tenant utility marks. Any visible personal utility mark will be labelled Tenant-recorded and not verified. The Manager will establish properties, billing-linked units and occupancy, verified utility mappings, rent settings, and individual or shared arrangements; handle sensitive corrections; confirm or reject rent payments; authorize eligible final-cycle advance application; and access confirmed rent receipts. The Manager may also perform operational tasks. Staff will work only within the assigned business workspace, update permitted descriptive details on existing records, upload utility bills, monitor intake, investigate exceptions, and record notes or escalations. Staff may submit one pending correction proposal per unfinalized incoming utility bill, with proposed values and a reason. The proposal will not alter live billing until the Manager authorizes it and the system confirms that the source and relevant billing context remain current and pass revalidation. Rejection, stale proposals, and failed validation will retain reasons and leave the proposed billing change unapplied. Previous values and the preparing and authorizing actors will be retained. Staff will not create billing-linked occupancy, modify login identity or financial settings, confirm rent, apply advance, or change Tenant utility tracking. Routine valid bills will continue automatically without Staff or Manager approval. Tenants will view their permitted records, report rent payments, maintain their own utility tracking marks, and receive permitted alerts. Authentication and role restrictions will protect centralized records. Evaluation will cover Functional Suitability, Performance Efficiency, Interaction Capability, Reliability, and Security under the selected ISO/IEC 25010:2023 characteristics. It will not establish long-term changes in revenue, profitability, payment compliance, or Tenant behavior.

Independent business workspaces will separate each management group's operational records. Managers and Staff will access only their authorized workspace, while Tenants will access their own records. Admin access will support authorized account and workspace maintenance and read-only inspection across workspaces, without operational editing or rent-confirmation authority. The Tenant calendar will display actual validated bill dates and clearly labelled estimates of upcoming configured rent dates. Estimates will not create charges, establish payment obligations, or predict utility dates. Workspace separation and calendar presentation support the included billing workflow rather than introduce new research objectives.

The study excludes mobile applications; installation or physical reading of smart meters or submeters; Internet or Wi-Fi billing; predictive profit analytics or billing; Generative AI and autonomous AI billing decisions; blockchain; automatic utility disconnection; payment gateways or bank integration; independent external payment verification; automatic access to provider apps or phone notifications; maintenance tickets; legal contract generation; and automated eviction. OCR will not cover handwritten, heavily damaged, severely distorted, or low-resolution documents. The study does not guarantee Web Push or email delivery or readership, establish a universally fair utility-allocation formula, or provide complete legal certification under the Philippine Data Privacy Act.
new:
Our study will develop and evaluate a web-based property-management workflow for selected boarding houses and residential apartments in Pasig City during Academic Year 2026-2027. It will cover rent, electricity and water billing, with access assigned to Admin, Manager, Staff and Tenant accounts. Admin will handle account and system maintenance and permitted read-only inspection. Staff will perform authorized daily tasks and prepare corrections, while the Manager will control financial settings, correction decisions and rent confirmation. Tenants will access their own records and permitted functions.

Our system will receive supported utility-email summaries and attachments, together with optional uploads of clear printed-bill photographs or scans. It will use direct text extraction or OCR to obtain billing details, validate them, identify the billing arrangement and calculate individual or equal shared charges. Processing will depend on readable supported documents and verified account mappings. Missing, masked, conflicting or otherwise invalid information will require review rather than guessed values or automatic finalization. Unsupported password-protected attachments will require review and an available supported copy. Routine valid bills will proceed automatically.

Rent functions will include fixed, non-prorated monthly anniversary billing, approved one-month advance handling for the final applicable rent cycle, payment reporting, Manager confirmation and confirmed rent receipts. Utility payment marks will remain personal Tenant tracking and will not establish provider settlement or produce utility receipts. Billing history, actual bill dates, labelled rent estimates, portal alerts, rent and utility Web Push, and supplementary rent-only email will support Tenant access. Rent estimates will not create charges or predict utility dates. Workspaces, basic reports, access controls, system-status checks and backups will support the included workflow rather than serve as separate research objectives. Detailed processing and permission rules are presented in Chapter II.

Our evaluation will use controlled conditions and selected properties. In the local setup, users will need a connection to the server's network; remote access will require a separately configured, reachable HTTPS address. The server must remain running for portal access and scheduled processing. Gmail retrieval and external notifications will require internet connectivity. The study will not establish readiness for large-scale deployment or guarantee continuous public availability, notification delivery or readership.

The study will exclude native mobile applications, smart-meter installation or reading, internet-service billing, payment gateways, automatic bank or provider-payment verification, provider-app access, SMS, predictive billing, model training, autonomous AI decisions, blockchain, maintenance tickets, automatic unit transfers or renewals, legal-contract generation and automated eviction. OCR will not cover handwritten, heavily damaged, severely distorted or low-resolution documents. Evaluation will address the five selected ISO/IEC 25010:2023 characteristics under the stated test conditions; it will not establish universal extraction accuracy, long-term business improvements or complete legal certification.
